review: One of my favorite SHMUPs ever. An incredible array of different ship & weapon types, beautiful 3D graphics & a soundtrack on-par with CastleVania. You can unlock the ability to play two ships at once, which is one of my favorite features in any SHMUP ever. Highly recommended.

A very interesting bullet-hell shooter. Every character has their own unique abilities and stories that make every playthrough feel different. This game is very difficult, even on Normal. Some of the bullet patterns are quite stylish. The shame break system is funny and a bit sus (you can turn them off in the options menu).

This game has Sol towers just like Raiden, and it also has two bonus stages that are great for getting extra resources a la Raiden IV Overkill and Raiden V: Director's Cut. Moreover, most of the weapons in Raiden V are available here which is awesome. The bullet patterns are not at all Raiden-like, though, as this game really tries to conform to its contemporaries.

A quick rundown of the three modes. Original Mode: 5 stages. No bonus stages. Special ability (press LT when all three abilities have 50% or more) clears the screen followed by a special, very powerful attack that lasts a few seconds.
Evolution Mode: 6 stages + 2 bonus stages. Special ability makes your three elemental shots more powerful.
Arcade Mode: 5 stages + 2 bonus stages. Special ability gives you unlimited access to your elemental shots for a limited time. This mode sucks.

Not a must-play imo, but it is very interesting to see Moss do their own attempt at a danmaku. Definitely could have used a sequel to flesh things out.

Caladrius Blaze es ese tipo de shoot ‘em up con sobredosis de esencia japonesa. Mucho anime, ataques complicados de esquivar y te hace sentir la tensión, es constante.

Y aun así… tiene un platino perfecto. De esos que no son injustos, pero sí brutalmente exigentes. Un platino que me encantaría tener en mi perfil de Steam… no obstante🍷 me he rendido.

[h2]Gameplay[/h2]

Es inmejorable en mi opinión, no le cambiaría nada.
Este juego tiene 8 personajes jugables y cada uno tiene ataques diferentes, o sea tiene una variedad de formas de jugar increíbles.
Aunque si esto hubiera sido como el Natsuki Chronicles del desarrollador Qute, estilo mejorar ataques por partida hubiera estado bien.
Pero esto solo se puede mejorar en la partida, esto mantiene más la tensión.

Además, contiene varios modos de juego, todos necesarios para el platino.
Aunque en esencia no cambia el gameplay sino los eventos.

[h2]Diseño[/h2]

Como bien sabrás, este juego combina el estilo anime 2D con un mundo en 3D, esto hace que las cinemáticas tengan mucha profundidad, algo que en lo personal me gusta en los shoot ‘em up.

Aunque claro, es un AA del 2013, no espere que tenga gráficos realistas ni nada, aunque le viene bien los gráficos que contiene en mi opinión, el realismo no combina tan bien con la estética anime que representa este título.
Por cierto, los dibujos son increibles, muy detallados.

[h2]Logros/Platino(100%)[/h2]

Este juego tiene un 7/10 de dificultad según PSNProfiles, este mismo menciona que tiene una duración aproximada de 35h, sin embargo… Steam Hunters le da un promedio de 22h al día de hoy.

Como mencioné antes, es un platino perfecto al modo que yo lo veo, contiene logros que te hacen aprovechar el juego por completo, cosas de llenar la galería y desafíos.
El motivo del porqué deje este videojuego sin completar es por lo que requería para el 100%, me pareció muy agobiante para mi gusto y quería dejar un buen recuerdo de este título.

Ahora, si a ti te encantan los juegos difíciles, seguro golpearas la mesa con este.
Yo si lo recomiendo.

Caladrius Blaze — это вихревой вертикальный скролл-шутер, где каждая битва взмывает до небес адреналина, а экран буквально пульсирует огнём и глазами уникальных персонажей с оригинальными способностями.

В игре ты сносишь волны врагов, фантастических боссов и постоянно ждёшь нового момента, когда всё вокруг разлетится в огненном хороводе, а экран запылает невероятными визуальными эффектами — настоящий праздник для фанатов классических аркад.

Особое внимание — на разнообразие героев и их стили стрельбы: каждый персонаж ведёт свой собственный «танец» с врагами, а выбор тактики превращается в мини-головоломку в гуще атак и лазерных залпов.

Игра смешивает ретро-дух и современные элементы: старые добрые нажатия кнопки «стрелять» соседствуют с продуманной системой улучшений и тактическими элементами, что делает процесс схваток бодрым, цепляющим и действительно затягивающим.

Мимо не пройти и шоу-эффекты: когда враг получает урон, ты иногда видишь не просто повреждения, а стильные арт-вставки с персонажами и боссами — неожиданная, но колоритная «визуальная награда» за успехи.

Хотя это может быть короткий и хардкорный стрелялка для глаз, Caladrius Blaze умудряется сочетать интенсивную аркадную динамику, разнообразие персонажей и эстетическую смелость, что делает её отличным представителем жанра для тех, кто любит стрелялки с характером.

I rate Caladrius Blaze 3.5/5. Pretty good. This is a vertically scrolling, arcade-style, shoot-em-up action game set in a high fantasy world wherein the unrestrained use of an ancient, evil, demonic spell has corrupted a kingdom. Characters mostly use flying vehicles but also have their portraits displayed at the sides of the screen. As characters take damage (both your own and enemy boss characters) their clothes get increasingly damaged, eventually getting shredded to the point of becoming extremely revealing (fan service style) though the most explicit details are never fully exposed.

Notes: 

*This game tends to assume you are using some sort of controller even though it works perfectly well with a keyboard. If an in-game menu tells you to press “A” you should just press either “Z” or the “ENTER” key.

*There are 6 firing buttons to bind (4 separate keys for firing your primary weapons and 2 other keys for firing bombs and a special move) and learning how and when to use them is key to understanding how to play this game well (beyond merely dodging enemies and enemy projectiles.


Good things about this game:

+ A Large number of characters are unlocked from the outset of the game (7 or 8 characters in total. I can’t remember whether one of them needs to be unlocked). The firing patterns of the different characters are different enough to help keep things somewhat interesting.

+Each character has their own dialogue with each of the game’s boss characters. This dialog ranges from being funny, silly to touching, metaphysical and highly philosophical depending on which character you play. The dialogue really is thought-provoking in some places, especially when it concerns issues of loyalty and faith. Caladrius Blaze’s dialogue and various endings and story is where this game truly shines, if you can manage to somehow overlook all the amazingly stereotypical anime-style voices that all the characters have.

+ Not a very frustrating game. You can continue after being killed an infinite number of times (doing so merely resets your score). Just press “ENTER” when the continue count down appears.

+ Fairly exciting boss fights.

+ Highly responsive controls.

+ Fairly interesting bosses and firing patterns.

+No major bugs or errors that I noticed.

+ Fan service clothes shredding! 

+ This game also has a pretty good steam profile background available of a sexy anime nun, if that’s your thing (and it can be fun to display if you want to mildly ruffle some straight-laced feathers). And yes, she is also a character you can play.


Mediocre things about this game:

+/- Each key can be rebound though the process for doing so is somewhat cumbersome.

+/- The game’s important dialogue has English subtitles. However, shorter phrases characters say when firing a powerful weapon are in Japanese without subtitles. There is no option for English audio dubbing. 

+/- The game’s intro animation is of such quality as to be worthy of a television anime series. Unfortunately Caladrius Blaze’s music won’t be for everyone. I found the music to be variously dull, overly frenetic and busy (yet with no strong musical theme) and sometimes outright irritating (as in the case of the game’s traditional (and very professionally done) anime-styled intro animation.

+/- Playing through the game repeatedly with different characters unlocks additional artwork and backstory and character profiles for you to look at from a menu gallery. I wish all this stuff was unlocked to begin with as playing through this game 8 times gets awfully repetitious and people who are such fans of this game shouldn’t be coerced (in any manner) into having to do this unless they really want to anyhow. The fun of playing the game with each character should be its own reward.


Bad things about this game:

- The levels themselves are only moderately interesting, most of them scrolling by in a fairly sedate manner (with a few exceptions). The smaller enemies (non-boss enemies) are also not particularly creative.

- Regardless of which character you play, the same bosses appear in the same order; they merely say different things to each character. There are 3 game modes but the chief difference between them, so far as I can tell is how many levels they include (the middle one in the menu has the most levels). Because of the lack of unusual modes to play and the bosses appearing in the same order each time, the game can feel repetitious after a short while (this is an arcade-style game after all), which is too bad because it really is fun and interesting to see all the character dialogue and some of it is quite good.

I wanted so badly to like this game. It has so many unique ideas and methods of execution, and the 'elemental shot' system alone seems like it should be enough fun to warrant a recommendation... but despite all of this, the game generally isn't fun to play, mostly because all of the difficulty is concentrated in the bosses, and from stage 3 onward they use some attacks which are flatly unenjoyable to dodge. Unless you like abusing your shield ability (and even if you do) there doesn't seem to be a good way to negotiate a large number of the boss attacks... and this gets worse and worse as the stages go on. One of the later stages also commits an unforgivable sin, in having a pair of homing drones chase you for the ENTIRE stage, meaning you can never stay in one place at a time or they'll pop up beside you and end your run. This is one of the coin-grabbiest pieces of design I've ever seen in my life, and given the lineage of the dev team, it really made me feel like this game is meant to be far more style than substance.

All that's a shame, because the element system, character design, and even storytelling--yes, the story is actually genuinely interesting for several characters--is far and above what I've seen in other games in the genre--it just doesn't matter when the actual game itself isn't fun to play.

If you think all the unique systems and weird quirks (don't get too excited for the clothing destruction, there's no proper H) sound interesting then this might still be worth a look, but ultimately I have to recommend avoiding it, despite many, many attempts to give it a shot.

Caladrius Blaze had more that didn't impress than did.  I found the wide array of abilities, the movement and even the various attacks for the many pilot options to just not hold my interest.  On top of each pilot of own little story that I skipped more than I half read.  The game never really came together to me, and I didn't find myself enjoying it much.

The primary mechanic that separates Caladruis Blaze from other shoot 'em ups is the Elemental Shot system.  Each of the many pilots have their own three special attack that drains energy from separate pools.  And at the end of a stage the player can increase the effectiveness of these elemental shots by allocating points into them. Additionally, characters have a bullet clearing bomb attack and a special.  Which I think for the pilots I've played, clear enemy bullets.  I'm not quite sure yet, as I'm still working the kinks out of mapping my controller.

The options are fine, I suppose.  The controller mapping isn't the best but also isn't the worst.  The difficulty I'm having comes the number of buttons the game uses and the re-mapping isn't a press button for that action.  Rather, a assign action to the 'X' button, then figure out which button on my controller the game thinks is the 'X' button.  This gets dicey when I get to the trigger buttons, and what the game considers triggers on my 8-button Sega Genesis controller.

Game play is not quite a vertizontal I think, but it's a long ways from Tate.  It's one of the few shmups I want to go with a faster ship to better cover the play area.  Since the slower ships struggle to get back and forth to get under enemies to destroy them.  I prefer simpler shooter mechanics, so I feel all the different shot types and everything over complicate and otherwise fairly simple game.  The meat of the stages had nothing that stood out to be other than the art style.  The enemies and bullet patterns on the non-boss stuff didn't grab me much.  

The boss fights were okay. I'm certain I'm not making the best use of all the tools at my disposal to dispatch them faster.  So, I found these fights to be a slog more often than not.  However, at no point did the game do anything to make feel like I wanted to get better at it.  So, just kept credit feeding my way through.

The graphics, sound and art design are nice.  Though, the game could have left out the 'shame break' stuff which I don't think added anything.  What I like was the world seemed to be the Gothic fantasy world that just so happened to have spaceship-type fighters in it.  I appreciate that the dialogue is voice acted, but as a non-Japanese speaker and not particularly interested in any of the character's stories I pretty much skipped pasted them.

Caladrius Blaze wasn't for me.  And because I couldn't find much that I enjoyed, I just can't recommend it.  Perhaps it has an audience that likes it far more than me.  And for the Summer Sale price I paid I don't feel bad about adding it to my collection.  It's not necessarily a bad game.  It's just not one that impressed me enough to clear the Recommend bar from me.  I found it a game of bits and pieces that never came together as a coherent whole quite enough for me to have much fun.

Il est super! Non sans défauts, mais pour le prix auquel je l'ai eu, c'est une bonne affaire. Fan de mangas, il n'y a pas à être déçus, tout juste si quelques couleurs n'était pas aussi prononcées. Mais à part ça, il est plutôt bien fait. Il y a un mode Full Screen, puisque la fenêtre de base sur mon écran, été de 1080P, mais avec le pleine écran, je devrais suivre plus facilement le mode histoire, puisque le vecteur principal du jeu- en dehors du fait que c'est un shmup, est qu'il y a une histoire. Classique, mais il y a une histoire. C'est en japonais, mais les textes sont en anglais, sur une petite fenêtre, c'est un peu difficile à comprendre, voir à lire...
Les amateurs de fan services, ne devraient pas être déçus, même s'il y a rien d'extravagant. Un jeu plutôt généreux, comme j'aimerais en voir beaucoup plus!  Je ne regrette absolument pas mon achat. La galerie s'étoffe aux fils des victoires, et c'est un petit plus. Il y a trois modes de jeux, je suppose rajouté au fur-et-à mesure. Rien à redire sur les animation, les flots d'ennemis ce présente, le tout sans problèmes de fluidités. Les bruits d'explosion auraient été mieux fait, que ça ne m'aurait pas dérangé. Ce jeu, me donne à penser à Ikaruga, la polarité en moins, quoique! C'est un Danmaku, et malgré que le jeu reste faisable, heureusement que j'avais les continus infinis, pour terminer l'histoire avec un personnage. Je verrais pour finir avec d'autres plus tard. Quand on est game over, si on poursuis à l'infini, le score redevient vierge lui. Un mode classique, pour faire son shmup est de la partie, sans l'histoire. Un jue de tir moderne, plutôt bien fait.

I stumbled onto the original game, Caladrius, on the Xbox 360, ages ago. After I started playing, I quickly began to realise that this game is, shall we say... risque? As you damage the bosses, or you take damage yourself, the clothes start to disintegrate, and there is a fair amount of skin flying around (no ACTUAL nudity, though). This version is less censored than the 360 version. Too bad you need both hands to play, huh, you little freaks out there.

THAT ASIDE.. this is one of the best shmups that I have ever played. I consider it to be as good as Gradius/Parodius. Solid gameplay, with good customisation. Eventually you can just pick your fav ship, and pick whatever subweapons that you prefer from all of the other ships. Very good arcade-style shmup action. No randomness, it's very much a "learn the pattern for each level" kind of thing. Very satisfying when you get it down. Worth your time if you're a fan of the genre, just mind them boobies around the family or at work.

[h1]脱げる雷電。[/h1]

雷電シリーズの開発メーカーによるキャラ推しの縦STGである。ベースとなっているのは雷電だが随分とカジュアルな方向に寄せており、1種類のメインウェポンと3種類のサブウェポンの4ボタン操作は指が忙しいが、これらのおかげでクリアしやすい難易度になっている。

日本語非対応のあれこれやUIの出来については散々語られているので省くが、本作は珍しく本当の意味で「初心者向けSTG」が体現できていると感じた。難易度選択も一番低いものにすれば本当にぬるく、自機選択もカラドリウスにすると笑えるぐらい楽だ。

個人的にこのゲームが面白いと感じる点は「カラドリウスの強さと他機体の強さの差」だ。

本作のプレイヤーキャラは女性が多めで一定条件を満たして被弾すると服が脱げていく。ボスも女性中心で形態変化のタイミングで服が脱げていく。そんな嬉しい仕様だ。しかしカラドリウスは最強の機体でありながら、見た目は「鳥」だ。喋る鳥なのである。脱衣なんてものはありゃしないのだ。なので「使用キャラの脱衣が見たけりゃカラドリウス以外も使いこなせ」という導線（制作の裏のメッセージ）が上手く出来ており、プレイを繰り返す動機付けになっているのが茶目っ気がありつつもちゃんと考えられている。

そして面白さの第二要因がサブウェポン3種類の付け替えだ。キャラごとにサブウェポンは3種あるが確か使用した機体でクリアすると（それが最低難易度だろうと）その機体のサブウェポンすべてが他の機体でも使えるようになるので「俺の考えた最強の組み合わせ」ができるという寸法だ。それによってバリアが強いサブウェポン、雑魚狩りに強いサブウェポン、対ボスで強力なダメージを与えられるサブウェポンを一つの機体に揃えることが出来て暴れられるというわけだ。あとはもうたっぷりとボスの服をひん剥けばいい。

幸い、本作は通常の難易度でも道中はぬるめでボスも殺しに来る攻撃は少なめなのでボムの決め打ちを心掛けていればノーコンクリアは他の雷電シリーズに比べればよほど楽である。ラストステージのしつこいビットは確かにきついが常に自機狙い弾を避け続ける感覚で動いていればなんとかなる。ラスボスもわからん殺しはあるが安定してラストステージに来れるならボムは余っているはずなのでボムのごり押しで倒してしまえばいいのだ。大丈夫、ラスボスにもちゃんとボムは効く。

余談として本作のイラストを担当しているヤスダスズヒトは[b]女性を巨乳に描く傾向が極めて強い[/b]が、[h1]本作も御多分漏れず巨乳だらけである。[/h1]
